summary:
Implemented the terminal window title setting in the rich repo; nothing committed and no tests, Black, or mypy run (edits verified by reading only).

Changes:
- rich/segment.py: added SET_WINDOW_TITLE = 16 after ERASE_IN_LINE; added Tuple[ControlType, str] to the ControlCode union.
- rich/control.py: added the CONTROL_CODES_FORMAT entry producing "\x1b]0;{title}\x07"; added Control.title(title), which returns cls((ControlType.SET_WINDOW_TITLE, title)), with a docstring including an Args entry.
- rich/console.py: added Console.set_window_title(title) -> bool beside show_cursor. It checks only is_terminal, buffers Control.title(title), and returns True; otherwise returns False with nothing buffered. Google-style docstring includes the restore/overwrite caveat and the "True means written" note.
- rich/_windows_renderer.py: new branch in legacy_windows_render that calls term.set_title(title) using the second tuple item. Win32 wrapper unchanged.
- CHANGELOG.md: Unreleased "Added" bullet linking pull request 2200.
- Tests: test_console.py::test_set_window_title (skipped on win32); test_control.py::test_control_title; test_windows_renderer.py::test_control_set_window_title (asserts set_title called once with "Hello, world!").

Choices: the Console test uses the sys.platform == "win32" skip marker, matching existing tests. The non-terminal return path has no test because the spec's test list did not include it.
